#2158. Five goals, eight assists: Wolves loan flop hits electric form with UEFA Champions League club

Wolves’ downfall has been widely credited to failed recruitment. In recent times, valuable assets like Matheus Cunha, Ruben Neves and Pedro Neto have been sold without suitable replacements coming in to keep the standards high at Molineux.

One player who struggled to fill gaps in Wanderers’ attack in the 2024/25 season was Carlos Forbs. The Old Gold brought him in on loan from Ajax, where he had struggled to hit the ground running after an exciting youth career at Manchester City.

Forbs’ time at Molineux did not go as planned. However, over the past 18 months or so, the Portuguese winger has hit flying form and is catching the eye in Europe.

At Wolves. Forbs played only 11 times across all competitions and contributed with one assist. He played just 16 minutes of Premier League football over the second half of his 2024/25 season and upon the return to Ajax, they decided to cash in.

Forbs was sold to Belgian side Club Brugge, and the 22-year-old has started to show why he was so highly rated in his youth. He performed well in his debut season with 11 goals and 12 assists in 51 games across all competitions and has taken things to another level this term.

In 15 appearances, Forbs has already notched 13 goal contributions with five goals and eight assists. He is starring in the Jupiler Pro League, but his success is really shown by his form in the UEFA Champions League.

The Wolves loan flop has two goals and three assists in four games in the prestigious competition. Club Brugge have won three games on the bounce in the Champions League, with Forbs setting up three goals in a 4-3 triumph away at Inter Milan before scoring in wins over RC Lens and PSV.

Forbs has been recalled to the Portugal first-team squad as a result of his surging stock.

Forbs’ fine youth career at Manchester City meant there was real excitement over his future. However, having struggled to make a telling impact at Ajax, it was perhaps a bit of an oversight to expect him to deliver in the Premier League at Wolves.

The Eredivisie is a strong league for player development, so the fact that Forbs struggled there suggested he had more progress to make before playing in the English top flight.

The winger has come on leaps and bounds in Belgium though. On his current form, it won’t be long before top clubs start to take notice.

#2156. Calciomercato no stop - Indiscrezioni, trattative e retroscena del 11 novembre

IL MILAN VUOLE TRESOLDI GIA' A GENNAIO. JUVENTUS, PER L'ATTACCO PIACE ANCHE SCAMACCA. NAPOLI, PER LA FASCIA L'OBIETTIVO NUMERO UNO E' CACCIAMANI. IN TRE POSSONO SALUTARE IL BOLOGNA. IL COMO PENSA A CAMELLO A GIUGNO. MANNA AMMETTE: "VARELA? IL MONZA NON LO CEDE". ROMA, ENDRICK E' IL GRANDE OBIETTIVO E LUI APRE ALL'ADDIO AL REAL MADRID. IL BESIKTAS DI ITALIANO SU SOLET E OKOYE. KVERNADZE, SPUNTA UNA CLAUSOLA DA 4 MILIONI VALIDA A LUGLIO

Il Milan getta la maschera e si butta sul mercato degli attaccanti ancora prima che arrivi l'estate: è infatti pronto l'assalto a Nicolò Tre­soldi. Ramos, pagato oltre 70 milioni di euro, non ha almeno per il momento curato il mal di gol del Milan, defi­cit di reti che era risul­tato deci­sivo già l’anno scorso nella man­cata corsa alla Cham­pions. Da qui l'obiettivo di inserire subito un innesto pesante, che porta appunto all'attaccante del del Bru­ges e (al momento) della nazio­nale tede­sca Under 21. Parlando di cifre, l'estate scorsa il Bru­ges ha rifiu­tato un’altra offerta ita­liana da 35 milioni (dalla Roma), e nel frat­tempo il prezzo si è impen­nato. In questa prima parte di stagione, compresa la nazionale, Tresoldi è già a quota 20 gol. Il costo dunque - sottolinea in questo senso La Gazzetta dello Sport - può aggi­rarsi ora intorno ai 50 milioni, un'altra spesa cla­mo­rosa se il Milan deci­desse dav­vero di affon­dare.

La Juventus è già proiettata sulla finestra di calciomercato di gennaio alla ricerca di un attaccante diverso da quelli che oggi Luciano Spalletti dispone in rosa e che possa tornare utile come faceva una volta Dusan Vlahovic (prima del trasferimento da svincolato al Besiktas). Se sul taccuino dei dirigenti Carnevali e Massara restano vivi i profili del norvegese Alexander Sorloth - chiuso all'Atletico Madrid da Jonathan David - e Folarin Balogun del Monaco, oltre al defilato Antonio Raimondo fermato da un grave infortunio alla caviglia al Frosinone, nelle ultime ore è emerso con forza il nome di Gianluca Scamacca. Lo riferisce TuttoSport. Le parti stanno studiando la fattibilità di un asse di mercato tra la Juve e la Dea, valutando un'operazione impostata sulla base di un prestito oneroso con diritto o obbligo di riscatto a condizioni agevolate da formalizzare in estate. L'attaccante romano, affamato di riscatto e desideroso di ritrovare un ruolo da protagonista, si ritroverebbe in una realtà bianconera esigente ma al momento in cerca di un giocatore come lui. E a Torino farebbe un bel salto dalla Conference all'Europa League, già conquistata in passato a Bergamo sotto la gestione Gasperini.

Il Napoli guarda anche ai giovani talenti della Serie A per rinforzare la rosa e programmare il futuro. Tra i profili finiti nel mirino della società azzurra c'è Alessio Cacciamani, esterno offensivo classe 2007 del Torino, protagonista di un ottimo avvio di stagione. Il diciannovenne, cresciuto nel vivaio granata, è un giocatore di piede destro che predilige partire dalla fascia sinistra. Le sue prestazioni hanno attirato l'interesse del Napoli, tanto che - si legge sul Corriere dello Sport - ci sarebbe già stato un contatto diretto tra Aurelio De Laurentiis e Urbano Cairo per sondare la disponibilità del club piemontese. L'operazione si preannuncia tutt'altro che semplice, soprattutto per la valutazione del cartellino. In estate il Torino aveva rifiutato un'offerta della Roma da circa 12 milioni di euro, fissando successivamente una richiesta superiore ai 20 milioni. Una cifra destinata a crescere ulteriormente alla luce del rendimento del giovane esterno, che ha collezionato 11 presenze da titolare nelle prime 12 partite tra campionato e Coppa Italia, realizzando un gol e un assist.

Il Resto del Carlino di oggi entra nel merito delle scelte di mercato per gennaio del Bologna: mister Palladino ha già fatto capire di voler avere un peso nelle scelte di gennaio e le parole di Fenucci fanno capire come i ragionamenti siano iniziati. Sono in tanti al momento gli scontenti tra i rossoblù: che il prestito di Dovbyk possa essere interrotto è una possibilità, visti anche i 3 milioni netti di ingaggio. Non solo. Se l’ucraino nell’ultima sosta rifiutò la convocazione dell’Ucraina convinto di poter scalare le gerarchie stavolta no, è partito. Ma la gestione Palladino ha raccontato anche altro: Ferguson e Pobega sono due titolarissimi. Neppure la settimana delle tre gare (una delle poche nella stagione senza Europa) ha visto Palladino offrire una chance da titolare a E Azzouzi o Moro. E se il primo è quantomeno entrato, il secondo continua a faticare a vedere il campo. Il quale in estate aveva una proposta da 3,5 milioni netti all’anno dagli arabi e che il Bologna ha trattenuto. Che il Bologna possa avere bisogno di un rinforzo lì nel mezzo, di un giocatore adatto a una mediana a due, è una certezza, perché prima o poi Palladino dovrà concedere un po’ riposo a Pobega e Ferguson.

L'anno scorso si è spinto fino alla finale di Conference League con il Rayo Vallecano, con 8 gol in 39 partite tra tutte le competizioni e solo uno in Europa. Oggi Sergio Camello sta trascinando la squadra di Vallecas nella Liga e si posiziona come sesto miglior marcatore del massimo campionato spagnolo, al pari di Fermin Lopez (Barcellona). Chissà se al termine della stagione potrà approdare al Como. C'è incertezza sul futuro dell'attaccante spagnolo. In primo luogo ha cominciato fortissimo la stagione (7 reti e 2 assist in 12 partite), con tanto di doppietta consecutiva tra il Barcellona di Lamine Yamal e il Racing Santander tra agosto e settembre. Polveri bagnate dal 19 ottobre contro il Getafe, solo un passaggio chiave vincente ai danni del Celta Vigo ultimamente e un feeling con il gol da ritrovare. Chissà se può centrare il rinnovo di contratto: non è ancora arrivato, anche se a giugno 2027 andrà in scadenza. Ergo, diventerà un succulento parametro zero. Tuttavia, senza un accordo con il club della Liga, a gennaio potrebbe presentarsi chiunque alla sua porta per tentarlo di un trasferimento. A giudicare dal valore dato al giocatore, da Vallecas pretenderebbero almeno un indennizzo per lasciarlo partire (a malincuore).

Giovanni Manna, direttore sportivo del Napoli, ha rilasciato una lunga intervista su diverse tematiche intervenendo ai microfoni di Radio Kiss Kiss. Queste le sue parole su Varela: "È un buon giocatore, ma noi adesso abbiamo Lucca, che è giovane e può ricoprire quella posizione. Il Napoli in questo momento è coperto. Poi vedremo, in base alle uscite, quello che succederà e faremo delle valutazioni. Sicuramente è un calciatore che sta facendo bene, con numeri importanti. Non penso che il Monza a gennaio voglia privarsi di un giocatore così, visto che lotta per la salvezza, e se lo farà sicuramente non lo regalerà. Noi in questo momento non ci siamo mossi, non abbiamo fatto assolutamente nulla. È un buon giocatore, ma il Napoli non ha fatto nessun passo”.

La Roma ha individuato nell'attacco il reparto da rinforzare con maggiore urgenza nella prossima sessione di mercato, che prenderà il via il 28 dicembre. Gian Piero Gasperini ha più volte sottolineato la necessità di ampliare le alternative offensive, mentre il direttore sportivo Tony D'Amico ha confermato: "Ci manca un esterno di gamba". L'obiettivo della società è mettere a disposizione dell'allenatore due nuovi attaccanti, mantenendo la linea già seguita in estate: calciatori giovani e ingaggi non superiori ai quattro milioni di euro annui. Secondo quanto riferisce Il Messaggero, in cima alla lista dei desideri c'è Endrick, già seguito a lungo durante l'ultima sessione estiva. Il ventenne brasiliano sta trovando pochissimo spazio nel Real Madrid, con appena 141 minuti disputati tra Liga e Champions League, impreziositi da un gol e un assist. Dal ritiro della nazionale ha lasciato aperta la porta a un possibile trasferimento: "Voglio solo giocare, essere felice e aiutare i miei compagni di squadra. Non so ancora che cosa accadrà, è tutto nelle mani di Dio. Chiedo solo ciò che è meglio per la mia carriera".

Vincenzo Italiano e il suo Besiktas guardano alla Serie A e, in particolare, alla rosa dell’Udinese per rinforzare la propria squadra in vista della sessione invernale di calciomercato. Il club turco avrebbe infatti individuato due profili per gennaio: Oumar Solet e Maduka Okoye. Lo riferisce TuttoUdinese.it, che sottolinea come l’obiettivo è intervenire soprattutto sul reparto arretrato, aumentando la qualità e la solidità dell’organico per compiere un ulteriore salto di livello e consolidare le proprie ambizioni.

Tra i giocatori che si stanno mettendo maggiormente in mostra nel Frosinone che è tra le rivelazioni della Serie A, occupa di diritto un posto l'esterno Giorgi Kvernadze (23 anni), autore fino a questo momento di 5 gol e 6 assist nelle 12 presenze che ha messo insieme con i ciociari tra Serie A e Coppa Italia. Inevitabile che su un profilo come quello di Kvernadze, classe 2003 e di talento, si stiano posando attenzioni in vista del prossimo calciomercato, quello di gennaio. Si è parlato del Napoli, per quello che però sembra al momento giusto un lieve interesse, ma soprattutto della Roma, che sulla ricerca dell'esterno d'attacco fonderà la prossima sessione di trasferimenti. La valutazione del Frosinone - che intanto lavora al rinnovo - è elevata, supera i 20-25 milioni di euro, anche se esiste pure lo spauracchio di una certa clausola. Cominciamo con un chiarimento: effettivamente nel contratto di Kvernadze con il Frosinone, in scadenza al 30 giugno 2028, è presente una clausola che permette di risolvere il vincolo con i gialloblù di fronte al pagamento di circa 4 milioni di euro di indennizzo. Una cifra al momento fortemente sproporzionata rispetto al reale valore del georgiano sul mercato, e anche per questo a Frosinone sembrano avere particolare premura di arrivare alla fumata bianca per il rinnovo (offerto 1 milione di euro netto l'anno, rispetto ai 200mila che percepisce ora). C'è però una specifica fondamentale, da fare, ovverosia che i gialloblù hanno ancora qualche mese a loro disposizione per arrivare a dama, considerando che la validità della suddetta clausola inizia solamente a partire da luglio.

CARRICK SARA' ESONERATO, IL PRESCELTO DEL MANCHESTER UNITED E' POCHETTINO. ATLETICO MADRID, INIZIATI I COLLOQUI PER IL RINNOVO DI SIMEONE. PRESTIANNI PUO' SALUTARE IL BENFICA: CI SONO PSG E BAYERN. CON POCHETTINO ALLO UNITED IL PRIMO OBIETTIVO DEGLI STATI UNITI COME NUOVO CT E' GUARDIOLA. LIVERPOOL, VAN DIJK VIAGGIA VERSO IL RINNOVO

Il destino di Michael Carrick al Manchester United è appeso a un filo. Secondo le ultime indiscrezioni provenienti dall’Inghilterra, il club avrebbe avviato contatti avanzati con Mauricio Pochettino per affidargli la guida tecnica nel caso in cui la società decidesse di interrompere il rapporto con l’attuale allenatore. Una decisione definitiva potrebbe arrivare già nelle prossime ore. I dirigenti Omar Berrada e Jason Wilcox si sarebbero recati a Montecarlo per un incontro con Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chiamato a decidere il futuro della panchina. Pochettino, attualmente commissario tecnico degli Stati Uniti, sarebbe favorevole a un ritorno in Premier League e avrebbe anche il sostegno della famiglia Glazer. L’argentino conosce bene il campionato inglese dopo le esperienze con Southampton, Tottenham e Chelsea.

L'Atletico Madrid e Diego Simeone hanno avviato i primi contatti per prolungare il loro storico rapporto. Il tecnico argentino, legato ai Colchoneros da un contratto in scadenza nel 2027, è la priorità assoluta della dirigenza e i dialoghi tra le parti sono già iniziati, con l'obiettivo di arrivare a un nuovo accordo. Il prossimo passaggio chiave è previsto nel mese di dicembre, quando club e allenatore si incontreranno per fare il punto della situazione e valutare i progressi della trattativa. Il clima è positivo e la volontà comune è quella di proseguire insieme, tanto che l'ipotesi di un prolungamento fino al 2029 prende sempre più quota.

Il futuro di Gianluca Prestianni potrebbe essere lontano dal Benfica, anche se non già nel mercato invernale. Lo riferisce il programma Record na Hora, affiliato al quotidiano lusitano Record, spiegando che l’esterno offensivo classe 2006 grazie alle sue prestazioni ha attirato l’attenzione di diverse big in Europa pronte a lanciare l’assalto in estate. I due club maggiormente interessati all’attaccante argentino sarebbero il Bayern Monaco, vista anche la questione Musiala, e soprattutto il Paris Saint-Germain che vedrebbe in Prestianni un calciatore con le caratteristiche giuste per affiancare Kvaratskhelia sulla corsia destra d’attacco della formazione di Luis Enrique. Il classe 2006 infatti non sarebbe visto come un sostituto del georgiano, ma di un innesto in più. Il Benfica valuta attualmente il calciatore, autore di 12 gol e 6 assist in 20 presenze, attorno ai 100 milioni di euro, una cifra che sicuramente non spaventa un club come quello parigino.

La Federcalcio statunitense (US Soccer) starebbe pensando a un grande nome per sostituire quel Mauricio Pochettino che potrebbe salutare dopo le due sfide di CONCACAF Nations League contro Haiti, valide per i quarti di finale, per approdare al Manchester United che lo ha scelto come sostituto di Carrick. Secondo quanto riferito da The Athletic, che cita fonti vicine alla US Soccer, il nome in cima alla lista della dirigenza sarebbe quello di Pep Guardiola, svincolato dopo l’addio al Manchester City in estate e che al momento non sembra però intenzionato a ripartire da una panchina tanto da aver rifiutato la proposta dell’Italia che ha poi virato sul ritorno di Roberto Mancini in panchina. Il catalano piace per le sue qualità di allenatore e l’esperienza internazionale accumulata allenando in tre nazioni diverse (Spagna, Germania e Inghilterra). Non è la prima volta che gli Stati Uniti pensano a Guardiola come allenatore. Già in passato infatti, dopo aver lasciato il Barcellona, il tecnico spagnolo aveva avuto contatti con la US Soccer nel corso del suo anno sabbatico a New York. Ma non solo altri contatti infatti ci sarebbero stati dopo il Mondiale del 2022 quando vennero contattati sia Guardiola sia Jurgen Klopp, ora ct della Germania, prima che la scelta ricadesse su Pochettino.

Nonostante negli ultimi mesi si sia parlato spesso di un suo possibile addio a fine stagione, quando scadrà il suo contratto, con diversi nomi di difensori centrali accostati al Liverpool, alla fine Virgil van Dijk potrebbe restare nel club inglese prolungando il contratto. Come riportano i media inglesi infatti il tecnico Andoni Iraola desidera che il capitano dei Reds resti nel club e sia ancora un perno della sua retroguardia. Per questo la società starebbe pianificando di offrire all'olandese un nuovo contratto .

#2155. Six goals in 11 consecutive wins: Ex-Norwich City man stars for European club after £14m sale

Norwich City bid farewell to Borja Sainz in the summer of 2025, following a fruitful two-year stay with the Norfolk outfit. NCFC signed the Spaniard from Turkish club Giresunspor and he enjoyed a steady first season with eight goals and two assists in 39 outings.

However, it was the 2024/25 campaign when Sainz would emerge as a real Championship star. The winger scored 19 goals and laid on four assists in 43 appearances for the Carrow Road club that season, prompting significant transfer interest before Porto paid a little over £14m to bring him in.

Sainz is now in his second season with the Portuguese giants. And, just like he did at Norwich City, the 25-year-old has grown into a starring role in his sophomore year.

Sainz had a solid debut year at Porto after joining from Norwich City, managing seven goals and six assists in 47 games across all competitions. He was not a nailed-on starter in Liga Portugal with 12 of his 30 league outings coming from the bench, but he settled well.

He has had to wait for his chances this term too, with all of his first eight league appearances coming off the bench despite scoring in three of those outings. Sainz has started the last three in the Portuguese top-flight though, and he has rewarded Francesco Farioli’s faith with three goals and an assist.

The ex-NCFC man has scored in back-to-back-to-back Liga Portugal games against Gil Vicente, Vitoria Guimaraes and Estoril, providing an assist against the latter too. He now has six goals and an assist to his name in 11 league matches this term.

Porto have won all 11 of those games to move into a commanding position at the top of the table. Sainz has made four appearances in the UEFA Champions League as well, but is yet to get off the mark in that prestigious competition.

Norwich City have had some real hits in the transfer market in recent times. Like Sainz, Gabriel Sara starred at Carrow Road and ended up earning a big move to Europe, while Mo Toure and Pelle Mattsson have become highly influential players at Carrow Road.

However, in terms of the money made and the level of success he found, Sainz takes some beating. He joined for nothing from Giresunspor and was sold for over £14m, making for a sizeable profit.

He’s gone on to prove his abilities after NCFC too, emerging as a key scorer at Porto. Sainz will be eager to keep delivering as Farioli and co see how long they can retain their perfect start to the Liga Portugal campaign.

#2154. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2153. Il Milan e Tresoldi: ha senso spendere 50 milioni per l'alternativa dell'acquisto più costoso della storia del club? Anche la Juve a caccia del bomber: di quattro centravanti in rosa non se ne fa uno. Varela sarà un nome caldo a gennaio

Non è un nome nuovo ma quasi: Nicolò Tresoldi è nel mirino del Milan. Il club rossonero ha puntato i suoi radar sull'attaccante italo-tedesco che ha fatto impazzire l'Inter in Champions League, segnando tre gol a San Siro nella vittoria del Brugge per 3-4 dello scorso 13 ottobre, e già a gennaio potrebbe preparare l'offensiva per provare a portare il giocatore nel club che ha sempre amato. Già, perché Tresoldi non ha mai nascosto il suo amore per la maglia rossonera, tanto che per lui, quella contro i nerazzurri, era una partita dal sapore di derby, ma riuscire a regalarlo ad Amorim sarà tutt'altro che semplice, visto che il valore dell'attaccante sta continuando a crescere, partita dopo partita. In estate la Roma provò a prenderlo, arrivando a offrire al Brugge 35 milioni di euro, offerta rispedita al mittente dai belgi, e visti i 20 gol già segnati in questa stagione, tra club e Nazionale Under 21 tedesca, dal centravanti, non è difficile capire che per acquistarlo potrebbero servire almeno 50 milioni di euro.

Questa domanda è giusto porsela. Non tanto per il valore dello stesso Nicolò Tresoldi e per quanto ancora potrebbe crescere, visto che stiamo parlando di un classe 2004, ma per il semplice fatto che proprio per quella casella del campo, soltanto pochi mesi fa, il Milan ha speso quasi 80 milioni di euro per prelevare Goncalo Ramos dal Paris Saint-Germain. Il portoghese, almeno per ora, non ha certo reso secondo le aspettative, ma sarebbe davvero producente spendere così tanto per l'alternativa al numero 9? Difficile dire di sì. Il Milan, comunque, avrà ancora tempo per decidere il da farsi e molto, se non tutto, dipenderà da come terminerà l'anno, relativamente ai gol, lo stesso Ramos.

Chi invece dovrà avere una strategia chiara che dovrà portare a un nuovo attaccante da affidare a Luciano Spalletti, è la Juventus. Attualmente, all'interno della rosa bianconera, ci sono quattro centravanti, o presunti tali: stiamo parlando di Randal Kolo Muani, Nick Woltemade, Jeff Ekhator e Arkadiusz Milik, tre dei quali sono arrivati proprio la scorsa estate. Di quattro, però, numeri alla mano, non se ne fa uno, e anche se sommando i loro stipendi ci si rende conto immediatamente che la Juve potrebbe permettersi Erling Haaland (stiamo scherzando, ma una punta di verità c'è), è inutile nascondersi dietro un dito: a gennaio servirà uno sforzo per regalare al tecnico una prima punta vera. Di nomi ce ne sono tanti, a cominciare da quel Sorloth che è tornato di moda, ma ce n'è anche un altro che, non per forza parlando di Juventus, finirà inevitabilmente al centro di tante trattative.

Il nome è quello di Gustavo Varela, attuale capocannoniere con la maglia del Monza in Serie A. L'amministratore delegato del club brianzolo, Mauro Baldissoni ha parlato chiaramente: "L'obiettivo è tenerlo con noi, il mercato è molto dinamico. Sappiamo che è ambito da club che hanno obiettivi più alti di quelli del Monza, contiamo di averlo con noi per tutta la stagione". Tradotto: il Monza vuole tenersi la sua stella, ma sarà praticamente impossibile farlo. Le società italiane non se lo facciano scappare, sarebbe un errore. E allora anche la Juve inizi a pensare anche a lui, così come tutti gli altri club che cercano un centravanti.

#2152. Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery said: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

“Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

While some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

It became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

After the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s

💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

Alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

The space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

Aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a big chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj

Doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

Two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

The teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes issues for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

Madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

Hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly new rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15

After Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I said that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away quickly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

In last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

This is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. New Villa signing Alejandro Garnacho has been ruled out tonight as part of the concussion protocols.

Garnacho was signed from Chelsea last month and took a whack to his face in the recent game against BG Pathum in Thailand.

Tonight’s game will be refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but got turned away at the border.

Team news is in 🔒 #PSGAVL pic.twitter.com/yeKkyIKiHQ

What will we learn from the “new Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

The Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a big summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

“I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

“No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

#2151. Finance expert alerts Sheffield Wednesday fans to Dejphon Chansiri development

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire has revealed an update on former Sheffield Wednesday owner Dejphon Chansiri's situation since being replaced at the club by David Storch and Arise Capital.

Dejphon Chansiri's turbulent ten-year reign at Sheffield Wednesday ended in October 2025 when severe financial mismanagement, unpaid wages, and mounting tax debts forced the club into administration. Following a six-month search for a buyer — and the collapse of an earlier bid — American consortium Arise Capital Partners, led by David Storch, emerged as the preferred bidder.

In May 2026, Storch’s group officially completed its takeover of both the club and Hillsborough Stadium, successfully persuading the EFL to waive a further 15-point penalty and closing the chapter on Chansiri’s divisive tenure. Now, more news Wednesday supporters will be keen to hear about has emerged.

Born into one of Thailand’s wealthiest families, Chansiri owes his fortune to the Thai Union Group, which is the world’s largest canned tuna producer. Though he held no executive role there, his personal ventures spanned Thai real estate, construction, and shipping — companies that largely struggled to generate significant profits.

Per the BBC, upon buying Sheffield Wednesday in 2015, Chansiri promised Premier League football within two years. He initially bankrolled heavy transfer spending through personal director’s loans and relied on external borrowing, including loans secured against Hillsborough.

However, after consecutive play-off heartbreaks, reckless overspending triggered Financial Fair Play breaches, points deductions, and relegation. Without sustainable income, his erratic, loan-heavy funding model eventually collapsed under mounting tax debts and unpaid wages.

The 25 top scorers in the Championship since the second tier was rebranded back in 2004/05, including Billy Sharp and Aleksandar Mitrovic.

It appears as though one of his business ventures has since collapsed a year on from his removal from Sheffield Wednesday after administration, with the bad news continuing for Chansiri after his energy drink company Blue Steel Beverages Ltd was dissolved, per Kieran Maguire.

For Sheffield Wednesday supporters, watching Chansiri’s post-Hillsborough business ventures unravel has to bring a strong sense of poetic justice.

After years of enduring unpaid wages, ticketing controversies, and the humiliation of administration, many fans have to openly savoured the recent news.

His UK-registered energy drink firm Blue Steel Beverages Ltd has finally been dissolved. The company’s quiet demise mirrors the fate of other elusive, Chansiri-linked brands, such as Elev8 and D Taxis, that famously adorned Hillsborough’s shirts and scoreboards without ever establishing a genuine commercial footprint.

For a fanbase long frustrated by his opaque financial dealings, seeing his side projects fold offers a satisfying footnote to his exit.

With the club now on the right path under Storch and Arise, they will hope Dave Challinor can return the club to the Championship by gaining promotion from League One at the first time of asking, with Chansiri then firmly in the rearview mirror at that stage.

#2150. New Southampton update can hand Millwall and Preston North End boost

Things were going so well for Southampton in the Championship - right up until last couple of games before the international break.

The Saints had well and truly put their four-point deduction from before the season began right behind them and had climbed up the table under Tonda Eckert, but a draw at West Brom, then defeat at lowly Preston North End last week saw momentum slow right down prior to the two-week break.

That loss was an unexpected one, and an early injury to Keven Schlotterbeck may have disrupted the steady nature of the Southampton defence, which saw little-seen Nottingham Forest loanee Zach Abbott come on for a rare appearance alongside Jack Stephens.

Southampton pounced late on in the summer transfer window to bring Abbott to St Mary's Stadium, signing the 20-year-old London-born defender on a loan deal until the end of 2026-27.

We've hit the second international break of the season - how does Opta think the rest of the Championship campaign will play out?

Capable of playing at right-back and centre-back, Abbott played 10 times across the Premier League and UEFA Europa League for the Tricky Trees last season, but with Oliver Glasner adding more defenders to his ranks over the summer, the youngster was sanctioned for a loan away.

Southampton though have not found a starting spot for Abbott, who had to wait until the October 14 clash with Norwich City for his first start - only to pick up a first half yellow card and was taken off at half-time by Eckert.

Relegated back to the bench after that, Abbott was handed a chance due to Schlotterbeck's unfortunate shoulder injury at Deepdale, and that could lead to another start after the international break.

Whether Abbott will be at Southampton for much longer though remains to be seen.

As per a report from John Percy of The Telegraph, Nottingham Forest are considering bringing Abbott back to the City Ground when the January transfer window due to his lack of minutes currently at St Mary's.

That of course could now change, depending on how long Schlotterbeck will be sidelined for, but Abbott will likely be competing with Nathan Wood for the spot next to Stephens in Eckert's starting centre-back pairing.

This Southampton fan thinks that it should actually be Abbott and Wood starting together, with Stephens dropped.

Another Saints supporter believes that Abbott showed enough against Preston - despite being on the losing side - to be given more opportunities.

Not everyone is in agreement though, with this particular Southampton fan wanting two new defenders in, and for Abbott to be sent back to Forest.

Given Abbott didn't play a competitive game for Forest this season before being sent out on loan, there's the opportunity for him to head to a new club if a recalled is triggered.

There were plenty of clubs keen to hand him the chance of playing Championship football, with two of those being Millwall and Preston North End, as per Alan Nixon's reporting in August.

And whilst neither club got him for the first half of the season, there could be renewed approaches in January given their situations.

Starting Millwall right-back Tristan Crama is struggling with injuries, having been restricted to just five appearances this season, and Abbott could potentially slot in there, giving the Frenchman a chance to partner Jake Cooper at the heart of defence once more when fit.

As for Preston, they've been extremely leaky this season and sit at the bottom of the Championship standings, and bringing in any sort of fresh defender - whether it's on the left or right-hand side - could be beneficial for Graham Alexander when January comes around.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#2149. Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

Aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

It was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward quickly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

You would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

The misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Whether it will be enough to keep him at Old Trafford for the long run remains to be seen, particularly as interest from Italy persists, but what can’t be doubted is his attitude. He looks sharp.

Manchester United 1 Leeds United 0 (Zirkzee) Leeds, on the attack, lose possession down the middle and Dorgu works it out to Mbeumo who beats Bijol 20 yards inside the Man Utd half. Leeds cross the free-kick into the box and James’ volley strikes a defender in the midriff and then hits the deck when going for the rebound, bundled over by Yoro. The ref waves play on and Manchester Unted counter with Amad Diallo dribbling down the right until tackled by Chadwick at the price of a corner.

Dorgu is penalised for a scissors-tackle on Bornauw. He did get the ball but only after he had caught he blond defender with his other leg. Carrick leaps up to protest, as does Farke but he is saying that Dorgu has twice slid in wildly.

Amad Diallo finds Mbeumo down the right and he tries to head the ball across the box but Muharemovic is well-placed to head it back out but an attempt to nod the ball back to Trafford goes astray and the £45m man can’t stop it going out for a corner.

Leeds free-kick for either a foul by Amass on Aaronson or Dorgu on Bogle. Hard to tell, one was a split-second after the other.

Amass pulls back Bogle after being tackled by the Leeds wing-back and Leeds build up the right from the free-kick, earning themselves a throw-in parallel with the penalty spot. In Ampadu’s absence Tanaka is the trebuchet, hurling in the long throw that Bornauw nods on but Manchester united clear the second ball.

Leeds work the ball back to Taafford from the kick off and he chips it long up the right. Dorgu heads it out for a throw-in. Leeds go backwards again and pass the ball around confidently.

Jaka Bijol captains Leeds, Diogo Dalot leads out Manchester United.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

It’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in New Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have new signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

#2148. Play: Taarabt's Dribble Dash

Few sights in Championship history are as fondly remembered as Adel Taarabt picking up the ball, dropping a shoulder and leaving a defender sitting on the turf.

The Moroccan playmaker had his critics, and his showboating could drive team-mates and managers to distraction. But when it clicked, there was nobody in the second tier quite like him. In 2010-11 it clicked like never before.

Neil Warnock took charge of QPR in March 2010 and over that summer decided to make the 21-year-old the focal point of his side. It proved a masterstroke.

Taarabt captained Rangers to the Championship title and was named the division’s Player of the Year after a season in which he scored 19 goals, helping the club return to the top flight after a 15-year absence.

He also picked up a place in the PFA Championship team of the season, and won QPR’s Goal of the Season for a superb solo effort against Swansea on Boxing Day.

Now it’s your turn to channel that magic. Taarabt’s Dribble Dash puts you in control of the QPR maverick as he runs at the heart of the opposition.

Swipe, tap or use your arrow keys to switch lanes, then weave past cones, lunging defenders and flying slide tackles on your way to goal. Every level ends with the ball rippling the net, and the further you go, the faster and more ruthless the defending becomes.

There are 15 levels to conquer, from a gentle warm-up session all the way to a nerve-shredding title decider. But you only get three lives for the whole run. Collect gold stars along the way for bonus points, and clear levels five and ten to win a life back. Chargers, trackers and sliding challenges will all be waiting for you before you get anywhere near promotion.

Can you guide Taarabt all the way to the title, or will you be scythed down on a cold, wet Tuesday night? Have a go below, then share your score on Facebook or X and challenge your mates to beat it.

And if you survive this one, try Escape from Neil Warnock elsewhere in our games hub.

In 2010-11 Adel Taarabt ran Championship defences ragged as QPR won the title. Now it’s your turn: weave him past cones, lunging defenders and flying slide tackles, and get the ball in the net at the end of each level. There are 15 levels and only three lives. How far can you take him?

A Football League World arcade game. Best played with sound on.
